aciklama: Gaziantep's legendary breakfast soup — thinly sliced lamb, rice, garlic and red butter in a rich bone broth. Eaten at dawn.
A warming winter stew of tiny hand-rolled meatballs and chickpeas simmered in lamb broth with dried herbs.
Tangy meatball soup sharpened with pomegranate molasses and lemon — a delicate balance of sour and savory.
Minced lamb and tail fat hand-kneaded with red pepper paste, grilled over charcoal and served on flatbread with sumac onions.
Fire-roasted eggplant blended with garlic yogurt, crowned with sautéed spiced lamb chunks. A dish fit for a sultan.
Ground meat blended with onion and spices, shaped into thick rings coated with sesame seeds and grilled on skewers.
Thinly sliced lamb liver marinated in red pepper and cumin, flash-grilled and wrapped in thin flatbread — a beloved street snack.
Alternating pieces of lamb and charred eggplant threaded on a skewer, basted with tomato and pepper sauce.
A Gaziantep exclusive — whole cuts of lamb shoulder slow-roasted in a sealed clay pot with onion and spices until fall-apart tender.
Crispy bulgur shell stuffed with spiced ground meat, pine nuts and walnuts — either fried or boiled in broth.
Paper-thin dough spread with a minced lamb, tomato and herb mixture, baked in a stone oven and rolled with onion and parsley.
Gossamer-thin dough layers folded over clotted cream (kaymak) and crushed pistachios, cooked on a griddle at dawn. Antep's most beloved breakfast.
Wafer-thin pastry sheets hand-rolled around a filling of ground pistachio and sugar, soaked in light syrup.
Pilaf made from fire-dried green wheat (firik) with lamb, giving a distinctive smoky, nutty aroma. A Gaziantep staple.
Tender vegetables (pepper, eggplant, squash) hollowed and filled with a spiced rice-and-lamb mixture, simmered in tomato broth until melt-in-mouth.
Dozens of hand-stretched phyllo layers, brushed with clarified butter, packed with fresh Antep pistachios and drenched in light syrup. The world standard.
Shredded wheat (kadayıf) sandwiching unsalted white cheese, baked in clarified butter until golden, soaked in syrup and topped with crushed pistachio.
Similar to baklava but crispier — phyllo triangles filled with clotted cream (kaymak) and pistachio, fried rather than baked. A morning treat.
Whole walnuts threaded on string, dipped repeatedly in thickened grape must until they form a firm, chewy molasses log.
Slow-reduced grape molasses, the backbone of Gaziantep cooking — drizzled on tahini, stirred into pastry dough, or eaten with bread for breakfast.
